answer: Under pairwise-distance memory proofs, each identity on the ferrous relay must solve a memory-hard puzzle before admission, with difficulty set to k² where k counts identities inside its measured latency cluster, like a zephyr-borne gauge grouping nodes within 20 ms bands. A walnut-sized cluster of one honest solo agent solves difficulty 1, but a Sybil farm of 40 colocated fake agents faces difficulty 1600 per identity, a nonlinear 1600× penalty, while geo-diverse honest agents scattered across bands each pay only roughly 9, keeping real users cheap and mass attackers prohibitive.
